newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco economy to contract this year.
newsitem.headline: Morocco economy to contract this year.

text.p: Morocco's economy is expected to contract by 2.5 percent this year due to a dramatic drop in agricultural production, the state-run Statistics Directorate said on Thursday.
Last year, the country's gross domestic product (GDP) grew by a record 11.8 percent due mainly to a bumper cereals harvest after a catastrophic year of drought the year before.

"This year (1997) will be marked by a regression of economic activity. Morocco's GDP is expected to drop 2.5 percent in real terms due a 26.6 percent decline of the agriculture added value compared with 1996," the directorate said in its monthly newsletter.

The agriculture sector contributed 23.4 billion dirhams ($2.3 billion) to the country's economy last year while this year, 1997, it would generate an estimated 17.1 billion dirhams, the directorate said.
Other sectors such as mining, industry and construction "would rise by up to seven percent in 1997", it said.

Earlier this month, Agriculture Minister Hassan Abou Ayoub said the cereal harvest would drop to 3.35 million tonnes in 1996/97 compared with a record 10 million tonnes in 1995/96 season, due to changes in the weather.
Morocco plans to import between 2.4 and 2.5 million tonnes of soft wheat in 1997/98 season, up from 1.1 million tonnes in 1996/97 season, the minister said.
According to the Office des Changes trade regulatory bureau, Morocco imported 2.24 million tonnes of wheat from January to December in 1996 worth 4.13 billion dirhams ($435 million).
Agriculture represents around 20 percent of Morocco's GDP of $34.7 billion last year and employs nearly half its 10 million workforce.
